newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says killed 26 Kurd guerrillas in clashes.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says killed 26 Kurd guerrillas in clashes.

text.p: Security forces killed 26 Kurdish guerrillas on Friday in clashes in southeast Turkey, bringing the rebel death toll this week to over 150, the emergency rule governor's office said.

A statement from the office, based in Diyarbakir province, said troops led an operation backed by air power against rebels from the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) on Cudi Mountain in the southeast province of Sirnak.
The statement did not refer to military casualties.
Elsewhere in the southeast, PKK guerrillas launched a rocket attack on Thursday night against a police station and military residence in Batman province, security officials told Reuters.
One soldier was injured in the attack, they said.
More than 100 people, including 12 soldiers, died in clashes between troops and Kurdish guerrillas earlier this week that spilled just across the border into northern Iraq.
A high-ranking security official said troops had entered Iraqi territory in the earlier fighting in pinprick raids but had later withdrawn.
On Thursday, the governor's office in Diyarbakir said 32 rebels had died in further clashes, mostly near the border.
More than 22,000 people have died in 12 years of conflict between troops and the PKK, fighting for Kurdish self-rule in southeast Turkey.
